headline: Gooble Review of Man's Childhood Home Posted by Someone He's Never Met
subheadline: Review describes house in detail he 'never shared publicly'; family denies knowing reviewer
summary: A deeply specific Gooble review of a private residence has left the homeowner's son searching for answers.
content:
A Gooble Maps review of a private residence has gone viral after the former occupant discovered it was written by someone who knows details about the house that were never made public.

The review, left by a user identified only as "M," rates the childhood home of Marcus Chen at 4 stars and reads: "Cozy three-bedroom with good natural light. The crack in the kitchen tile from 1994 adds character. Basement gets cold in winter but the water heater makes a comforting sound. Would recommend, but the tree in the backyard is not what it seems."

Chen, who moved out in 2003, was alarmed. "The crack in the kitchen tile—that happened when I was eight. We never reported it, never photographed it, never told anyone. How does this person know about the crack?"

His family has denied knowing anyone named "M" or sharing information about the house. The current owners, contacted by reporters, were unaware a review had been posted and expressed discomfort that someone had "rated their home."

"We didn't ask to be reviewed," the current homeowner said. "Also, what's wrong with the tree?"

Attempts to contact reviewer "M" have failed. Their Gooble profile contains no other activity—only this single review of a house in suburban Ohio, posted 18 months ago.

"The tree thing is what gets me," Chen said. "I always felt weird about that tree as a kid. Like something was off about it. But I never told anyone. Never even really articulated it to myself until I read this review."

The review has 847 "helpful" votes. One comment, from another anonymous account, reads only: "The tree knows too."

Gooble has declined to remove the review, stating it "does not violate content policies." When asked if reviews of private homes by unknown parties were normal, a spokesperson said: "Define normal."
author: Chris Patterson, Human Interest
